sourceSop: AI Content Authority Building SOP v1.0

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Transactional local repair diagnosis for broken, stuck, noisy, or unsafe garage doors.
factsWithContext: Most repair searches start from a symptom, so the page should map symptoms to likely repair paths.
City pages own local repair intent while service hubs own broader repair education and conversion.
Repair pages should separate urgent stuck/crooked doors from tune-up-level noise or minor sensor issues.
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Run live SERP overlap checks for the primary repair term in each city before adding more repair variants.

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Broken spring diagnosis, safety guidance, replacement expectations, and same-day repair conversion.
factsWithContext: Spring pages should explain that the opener is not designed to lift the full door weight after spring failure.
Cycle rating matters because heavy daily garage use changes the right spring recommendation.
Two-spring doors usually need paired replacement because both springs share the same cycle history.
supportQueries: what to do if garage door spring breaks
how to know if garage door spring is broken
cost to replace garage door spring
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Compare spring repair, broken spring, and spring replacement SERPs to decide whether replacement deserves a separate page family.

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Torsion-specific replacement and balance guidance for springs mounted above the door.
factsWithContext: Torsion intent is narrower than generic spring repair and should explain how the above-door assembly works.
Wrong sizing leaves the door unsafe even when the new spring is installed.
Manual balance testing is the practical proof that the repair was completed correctly.
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Check whether torsion spring repair and replace torsion spring are the same SERP in each active market.

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Opener motor, remote, keypad, sensor, gear, and force-setting troubleshooting that converts to repair calls.
factsWithContext: Opener pages must distinguish true motor failure from door balance problems.
Sensor and travel-limit issues often mimic opener failure and should be explained before replacement.
The hand-lift test is the decision point between opener repair and counterbalance repair.
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Check if sensor, keypad, and remote problems deserve separate PAA or service pages after GSC data appears.

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Urgent repair for stuck-open, stuck-closed, jammed, unsafe, or exposed garage doors.
factsWithContext: Emergency pages should prioritize the first safe outcome before explaining the final repair.
The same symptom can come from spring, cable, track, sensor, or opener failure, so the page should route by urgency.
Stuck-open and car-trapped calls are separate user pains even when they share the emergency repair cluster.
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Use GSC to decide whether stuck-open and stuck-closed deserve local city-service page families.

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Crooked, jammed, or off-track garage door repair with safety and damage-prevention guidance.
factsWithContext: Off-track pages should warn against running the opener after a roller leaves the track.
The content should connect off-track symptoms to cable, roller, hinge, and impact causes.
Panel inspection matters because a twisted door can create hidden damage.
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Check if bent track repair and off-track repair are separate SERPs before adding track-only pages.

activeClusters.primaryIntent: Snapped, loose, frayed, or drum-jumped cable repair for crooked or stuck garage doors.
factsWithContext: Cable pages should explain that one loose cable is a balance problem, not a cosmetic wire problem.
Pair replacement is often appropriate because both cables carry the same cycle load.
Cable failure can quickly become panel or track damage if the opener keeps running.
supportQueries: why did my garage door cable snap
what is the wire on my garage door called
activeClusters.nextSerpRefresh: Compare cable repair, cable replacement, and cable came off SERPs before adding new variants.

plannedClusters.reason: Installation and replacement are monetizable but should not be generated until live SERP overlap confirms the correct split.
Sensor intent appears inside opener repair today; create only if GSC shows distinct impressions or SERP overlap is low.
Noise, rollers, and hinges may be a maintenance cluster, but it needs SERP and GSC confirmation before page expansion.
